clue.text: Seat once popular though with no support

definitions.text: Seat once popular though with no support

parts.words: Seat once popular though with no support
parts.note: a floppy seat that was all the rage in the 1970s, filled with pellets and having neither legs nor a rigid back to hold the sitter up

explanation.surface: A wistful note about a fashionable chair that never held anyone up properly.
explanation.definitionFit: A pellet-filled sack used as a chair was a fashionable seat in its day and offers no frame or back support.

clue.text: Unusually large part of vehicle

definitions.meaning: a ... crop or harvest is an exceptionally big one
the bar across the front or back of a car that absorbs knocks

explanation.surface: A car part described as oversized.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumper means exceptionally abundant, as in a bumper year, and is also the shock-absorbing bar on a car.

clue.text: Agree to take on board

definitions.meaning: to agree to something is to consent to it
to take an idea on board is to embrace or receive it

explanation.surface: Consenting to load something onto a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are synonyms: consenting to a proposal and receiving or embracing an idea.

clue.text: "The narrow way": the clergy's material

parts.note: a playful contrast: the Gospel sets the narrow way to life against the wide road, so the quoted phrase points to its opposite, wide
the cloth is a collective name for the clergy, as in a man of the cloth

explanation.surface: A churchy quotation about the straight and narrow path, followed by talk of clerical vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: In Matthew's Gospel the narrow way leads to life while the broad way leads to destruction, so the quoted phrase suggests its opposite. 'The cloth' is a standard name for the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcloth is a fine, densely woven woollen or cotton fabric, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Blunder by the boss not reaching a conclusion

indicators.note: stopping short of the end means the final letter of the word for the boss is dropped

parts.note: gaffer is British slang for a boss or foreman

explanation.surface: A mistake made by the manager, who never got to the end of the matter.
explanation.walkthrough: GAFFER, everyday British slang for the boss, loses its last letter R.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social or diplomatic blunder, an embarrassing slip.

clue.text: Oil pact renegotiated? That's newsworthy!

indicators.note: a deal that is renegotiated has its terms rearranged, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A headline about an oil agreement being reworked, which is presumably big news.
explanation.definitionFit: Something topical concerns current affairs, so it is of interest to the news.

clue.text: Chunter on, rambling in the club

indicators.note: talk that rambles wanders all over the place, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling on and on, at length, in their club.
explanation.walkthrough: To chunter is British for to mutter or grumble; the surface sets 'club' as a members' club, but it is a cudgel.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short thick stick carried as a weapon, a type of club.

clue.text: American friends not right in cricket gear

indicators.note: the word not tells us the letter for right is left out

parts.note: pards is American slang for partners or pals, short for pardners

explanation.surface: Some American pals turning out in the wrong kit for a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: PARDS, US slang for partners, loses R. Cricket batters strap padded guards to their legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Pads are the protective leg guards worn by batters and wicketkeepers in cricket, so they are part of a player's gear.

clue.text: Agree money to go on drink mainly

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece going on another sits above it, so the coin comes first

parts.note: a coin is a piece of money

indicators.note: most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic drink made from apples

explanation.surface: Consenting to spend cash on a round of drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinions or accounts that coincide are in agreement, matching one another exactly.

clue.text: Boats being slimmer, bow to stern

indicators.note: a nautical way of saying front to back: the first letter goes to the end

parts.note: slighter means more slender or slimmer

explanation.surface: A remark that boats with narrower hulls handle better from front to back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow to stern' moves the S of SLIGHTER from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighters are flat-bottomed barges used to ferry goods to and from ships in harbour.

clue.text: Proud male doctor suffering endless pain inside

indicators.note: the trimmed word for pain is placed within the doctor's letters

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a standard abbreviation for a doctor

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: an ache is a dull persistent pain

explanation.surface: A swaggering man who is a doctor carrying some inner pain.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, for medical officer, is a common crossword abbreviation for a doctor; 'suffering' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A macho man is one who is assertively, often boastfully, masculine.

clue.text: Abandoned child discovered by Heather

parts.note: found means discovered or came upon
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: A deserted baby was found by someone called Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital H makes Heather look like a person's name; it is the moorland plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundling is an infant abandoned by its parents and then found and cared for by others.

clue.text: Ploy of former lover to deny epic mistake

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: read as a verb, to mistake these letters is to get them wrong, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ex-partner's scheme to deny they made a monumental blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' looks like a noun but signals an anagram of DENY EPIC, giving PEDIENCY.
explanation.definitionFit: Expediency is acting for advantage rather than principle, so a ploy or convenient manoeuvre fits it loosely.

clue.text: Old tax — of course, not the first

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word is to be removed

parts.note: Ascot is a famous English racecourse

explanation.surface: A historical levy, of course, though not the first one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' reads as a throwaway phrase, but 'course' is ASCOT, the Berkshire racecourse, which loses its A.
explanation.definitionFit: Scot was a medieval tax or levy, surviving in the phrase scot-free.

clue.text: Tester gets support here

parts.note: a tester is the canopy over a grand bed, held up at each corner by an upright

explanation.surface: A trial runner is backed up somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tester' suggests someone running trials; it is an old word for a bed canopy.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of bed has an upright at each corner holding up a canopy, known as a tester.

clue.text: Tenant not starting to please owner

indicators.note: not beginning means the first letter of the next word is left off

parts.note: a holder is someone who owns or possesses something

explanation.surface: A renter asking the landlord, with no please, for something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not starting' drops the P of 'please'; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaseholder occupies property under a lease from the freeholder, so is a kind of tenant.

clue.text: A stupid judge gives report in outline

parts.note: dumb is informal for stupid
to rate is to judge or assess

explanation.surface: A dim-witted judge produces only a sketchy report.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to sketch or indicate in outline, giving only a faint account.

clue.text: Cricket side finished, put out

parts.note: the off side is one half of a cricket field, facing the batter's bat
ended means finished

explanation.surface: A cricket team has completed its innings and been dismissed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' looks like a cricketing dismissal, but means upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put out is to be annoyed or upset, the same as feeling offended.

clue.text: Moving into pang treatment

indicators.note: giving the letters treatment works them over into a new order

explanation.surface: Treatment for a sudden sharp pain is underway.
explanation.definitionFit: Poignant describes something that evokes a keen sense of sadness, deeply touching or moving.

clue.text: Show sort of bean considered most likely to win the competition

definitions.text: considered most likely to win the competition

parts.note: a front is an outward show or appearance
the runner bean is a common climbing bean

explanation.surface: An exhibition variety of bean is tipped to take the top prize at the vegetable show.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a garden show, but 'Show' is FRONT, a facade.
explanation.definitionFit: A front-runner is the contestant who leads or is favourite in a race or contest.

clue.text: A tree by the sea in France is better established

parts.note: a fir is a type of tree
mer is the French word for sea

explanation.surface: A tree growing by the French coast is more securely rooted.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmer means more solidly fixed or settled, so better established.

clue.text: Man attracted to article

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
drew means attracted, as a crowd is drawn

explanation.surface: A fellow was drawn to a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; the charade is AN then DREW.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrew is a man's name, the generic first-name sense crosswords use for a man.

clue.text: So ring after a bit of work

indicators.note: the ring's letter comes after the unit of work

parts.note: an erg is a small unit of work or energy in physics
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: A wedding band given once a little job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, used in English to mean so or consequently.

clue.text: Ragged beard on a Scotsman — this one?

indicators.note: a ragged beard is unkempt and messy, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, these eight letters are the anagram fodder; the setter's fodder needed an extra I and N to fill all ten squares

explanation.surface: A northern Scot with a scruffy beard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ragged' signals an anagram, but BEARD ON A gives only eight letters; the answer also needs I and N, which nothing in the clue as printed provides.
explanation.definitionFit: An Aberdonian is a native of Aberdeen, a Scotsman of the type the scruffy beard suggests.

clue.text: Odd kind of degree in dance

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a university degree

explanation.surface: A strange sort of qualification awarded in dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance in four-four time.

clue.text: Incomplete country feature

indicators.note: not complete, so the final letter of the country is missing

parts.note: China is a country

explanation.surface: An unfinished feature about a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: The chin is part of the face, and facial parts are called features.

clue.text: Stop here for photography

parts.note: in a camera a stop is the adjustable aperture that controls light, made by an iris-like disc

explanation.surface: A sign at a scenic viewpoint inviting visitors to pull over and take pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop here' reads like a road sign; in photography a stop is the lens aperture setting.
explanation.definitionFit: In a camera lens the adjustable disc that sets the aperture, or stop, has this name.

clue.text: River artist on the carpet making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the whole run is read backwards
the artist's letters sit on top of the carpet's

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a standard abbreviation for an artist
a mat is a small carpet

explanation.surface: A painter who was reprimanded is staging a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the carpet' suggests a telling-off; 'making a comeback' turns RAMAT round. The Tamar divides Devon from Cornwall in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tamar is a river in south-west England forming most of the Devon-Cornwall border.

clue.text: Make river flow round temporary home for relaxation

indicators.note: a river flowing round something encloses it, so the tent goes inside

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England
a tent is a temporary shelter

explanation.surface: Campers diverting a stream past their tent to have a restful time.
explanation.definitionFit: Détente is an easing of tension between states, a relaxation of hostility.

clue.text: High-fliers broadcast on station (not English)

indicators.note: the broadcast piece comes on, before, the station's letters

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

indicators.note: the letter standing for English is left out

parts.note: Crewe is a major English railway junction station

explanation.surface: Something aired on a station that is not English.
explanation.walkthrough: CREWE, a famous railway junction in Cheshire, England, loses E.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircrew are the people who fly an aircraft, literally high-fliers.
